_doc: Named structural mechanisms the book argues for. Each mechanism has a clear definition site in the notes (`definedIn`) and is discussed in one or more chapters (`coveredBy`). `derivesFrom` captures derivation between mechanisms (e.g. medium-shapes-want derives from want-as-prime-mover). Aliases will drive an auto-alias matcher in a later phase.

mechanisms.label: Transport
mechanisms.summary: Lossy re-encoding at each stage of an abstraction pipeline. Each hop is a sender re-encoding for a new receiver; cumulative compression bounds how much complexity can survive transit. The telephone-game intuition.
mechanisms.plain: Each retelling of an idea for a new audience loses something, and what goes first is usually the fine print on how to read it.

passages.section: The two views
What a message is made of
Transport is a cost; selection is a choice

mechanisms.label: Selection
mechanisms.summary: Gates with local fitness criteria at each pipeline stage. What survives is whatever wins on emotional resonance, identity reinforcement, status, action affordance, novelty. Dominant constraint in modern digital networks where transport cost has collapsed.
mechanisms.plain: At every step, someone or something decides which ideas get passed on, and that decision follows rules that people can set on purpose.

passages.section: What the gate rewards
Transport is a cost; selection is a choice
The sibling pipeline: selection

mechanisms.label: Want as the prime mover
mechanisms.summary: Want drives a feedback loop where engagement accumulates preconditions that deepen further want. Both transport capacity and selection criteria are downstream of cumulative wanting. Reframes transport and selection as aspects of one dynamic, not two competing mechanisms.
mechanisms.plain: People only build the background that hard ideas need if they keep wanting to engage, so appetite comes before both ability and taste.

passages.section: Modality, not primacy
Three things the medium does to a gate

mechanisms.label: Medium shapes want
mechanisms.summary: Different media cultivate different kinds of want in receivers. A medium that rewards shallow engagement trains preconditions for shallow content; a medium that rewards sustained engagement does the opposite. McLuhan's 'the medium is the message' restated at the want-formation level.
mechanisms.plain: The places where we read, watch and scroll slowly train us to want more of whatever they reward.

passages.section: Three things the medium does to a gate
The medium selects wants; it doesn't author them
Modality, not primacy

mechanisms.label: Manufactured injection
mechanisms.summary: Content generated wholesale, never measured against reality, injected at later pipeline stages — astrology, conspiracy theories, propaganda, AI-generated text. Downstream selection criteria cannot easily distinguish measured from manufactured content.
mechanisms.plain: Some of what circulates as information was never checked against the world at all; it was made up and dropped into the stream partway down.

passages.section: Where manufactured content enters
The manipulation surface is the gate itself
The edge of the map: manufactured content

mechanisms.label: Interpretive latitude
mechanisms.summary: Stripping an idea's outer message does not fix a single wrong decoding key — it unpins the key, leaving the surviving claim underdetermined. The more compressed the claim, the wider the range of readings it will support. Compression's second effect, alongside shifting the expected decode: it widens the variance of decodes across receivers.
mechanisms.plain: The shorter a claim gets, the more different things people can take it to mean.

passages.section: Compression unpins the key
From latitude to segmentation
Three things compression can do to truth

mechanisms.label: Engagement-maximization as a captured equilibrium
mechanisms.summary: Engagement maximization is not an attack on the platform from outside — it is the platform's own business model acting as the captured selection-tuner. The metric being optimized (time-in-medium → ad inventory → revenue) is a proxy for revenue dressed up as a proxy for user benefit; the gate-criteria tuned to it converge on identity, threat, and high-arousal content because that is what holds attention. The equilibrium is the institution's normal operation, which is what makes it more stable than any externally captured institution — there is no adversary to defeat, only an arrangement to dismantle.
mechanisms.plain: A feed that sells your time keeps showing whatever holds you longest, and nobody has to intend any harm for that to happen.

passages.section: What engagement actually measures
Two kinds of capture
Where I land

mechanisms.label: Myth dilution at scale
mechanisms.summary: The loop by which a network's binding myth loses determinacy as the network grows: scale forces the myth to compress (complexity ceiling), compression widens its interpretive latitude, latitude sorted by community and identity gates segments the network, and segmentation forces the bureaucracy that re-supplies the dropped decoding key. A myth's reach and its determinacy trade off; whether the loop then compounds safely, fragments, or inverts into scale-as-control is set by the repairing bureaucracy's own resistance to capture.
mechanisms.plain: The bigger the group a shared story has to hold together, the simpler the story must get, and the more ways people can read it.

passages.section: A myth dilutes as its network grows
Bureaucracy is downstream of the myth
What decides the loop

mechanisms.label: Constitutive transmission
mechanisms.summary: How the pipeline operates on intersubjective cargo: each receiver's decode is a unit of the agreement whose being-held is the truth, so transmission participates in the generator rather than reporting on it. Reach changes the truth itself (the billionth holder of a currency adds to its value rather than learning about it); coverage feeds what it covers (the bank-run loop, where propagating 'the bank is failing' performs the failure); and the pipeline's clock rate becomes the constitution's volatility. The intersubjective sibling of transport: not moving a fact but compounding a generator.
aliases: the pipeline wired into the generator
mechanisms.plain: When something is real only because people agree on it, every retelling adds to or drains the agreement, so spreading the news changes the thing.

passages.section: The pipeline is wired into its own cargo
Constitutive volatility: the thesis's second blade
A fifth story: money

mechanisms.label: Framework pricing
mechanisms.summary: How a framework biases the thinking done inside it: it sets a price on every thought. Some operations are cheap, others laborious (cost asymmetry); one arrives free if nothing is chosen (the default); a few are off the menu because the framework cannot record them (legibility). No individual is forced, but across a population and over time the cheap thoughts win and conclusions carry the framework's shape. It is selection running inside one head with ease as the reward, and it is the weak-form replacement for 5b's 'a variant the option space cannot hold never forms': the variant rarely forms because it is expensive. Because it is a price, it can be paid (effort, training, subsidy, a second framework). Provisional; rests on the frameworks report.
aliases: the price list, not the wall

passages.section: What a framework does to a thought
The price list, not the wall

mechanisms.plain: A framework makes some thoughts cheap and others expensive, and across a whole population people mostly think the cheap ones.

mechanisms.label: Framework feedback
mechanisms.summary: The loop in which a framework's outputs are acted on and the world changes in response. It can run toward the framework (Barnesian performativity: Black-Scholes 1976-87; scientific forestry making the Normalbaum real) or away from it (counterperformativity, Goodhart/Campbell corruption of targeted measures, Hacking's looping kinds, Waldsterben). The book's claim: this is where framework bias does its real damage, because a map that is acted on rebuilds the ground and erases the mismatch that would have exposed it. The general form of constitutive transmission, and it reaches further: the forestry case shows managed objective reality being rebuilt to fit a map, which strains the truth-generators carving. Provisional; rests on the frameworks report.

passages.section: When the map starts moving the territory

mechanisms.plain: When people act on a framework's picture of the world, the world changes, sometimes to match the picture and sometimes to break it.
